newsitem.title: CANADA: Missing Canadian rescue crew found.
newsitem.headline: Missing Canadian rescue crew found.

text.p: The four crew members of a missing Canadian search-and-rescue helicopter were found Thursday more than 30 hours after they crashed in frigid waters off remote Labrador.

"They spent a couple of nights in pretty bad conditions up there," said Lt. Cmdr. Glenn Chamberlain of the Halifax Rescue Co-ordination Center. The men were taken by helicopter to a medical center in Kuujjuaq, Quebec to be treated for frostbite and crash-related injuries but their lives were not in danger, Chamberlain said.

They disappeared Tuesday night when bad weather forced them to abandon a rescue mission in Baffin Bay off Canada's windswept northeastern border between Baffin Island and Greenland. As part of that rescue, two Canadian military search-and rescue technicians parachuted from a Hercules aircraft into Baffin Bay's frigid waters Tuesday and swam to the ship to treat a seriously ill man aboard a trawler.

The Griffon helicopter was dispatched to airlift the man and his rescuers from the trawler but could not reach the scene because of snowy, windy weather. The patient and the two other rescuers were taken off the trawler by another vessel.

The helicopter landed in northern Labrador on Canada's east coast Tuesday night to wait out the storm but later left that location and was not heard from again. Chamberlain said it was too early to determine what went wrong with the aircraft, which was heading for a fuel cache when it crashed.

Although it was equipped with emergency location and satellite communications equipment, the crew was unable to send a distress signal because the helicopter sank offshore. The men were able to swim to shore and find refuge in a cabin.

The crew of a Canadian forces Hercules rescue aircraft saw the downed crew's emergency flares early Thursday. The Griffon crew included two pilots, a flight engineer and a memebr of a highly trained group of Canadian military specialists who conduct search-and-rescue missions across a vast territory that includes the Candaian Arctic.
